title: Measured movie similarity retained a contact-count link after two model controls in one MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested whether measured movie-response similarity retained a link to multiple synaptic contacts after two digital twin similarity measures were included. We used 8,128 connected pairs from one MICrONS mouse. A linear model controlled separate source and target cell effects and anatomical proximity lengths. The graph core had 5,158 pairs. The measured-response estimate was 0.53 percentage points per standard deviation, with a nominal 95 percent dyadic interval of -1.37 to 2.44. The two model-derived estimates had intervals that included zero. Source deletion and three outcome or control checks retained a positive measured-response estimate. These are conditional associations in selected connected pairs. They do not compare measurement quality, prove a causal effect, or show transfer across mice. Code, selected data, source hashes and numerical checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Separate and joint similarity slopes with cell and anatomical proximity controls. Bars give nominal 95 percent dyadic intervals in one selected mouse sample.
